metadata.title: Top Cybersecurity Stocks to Watch, According to Mizuho

content.text:
Investing.com -- Mizuho has released its latest rankings of top-performing cybersecurity stocks, with analysts highlighting strong momentum across multiple companies based on quarterly channel checks and partner feedback. The firm's analysis points to robust demand for data warehousing, zero trust solutions, and cyber-resiliency products.
1. Snowflake (SNOW) - Mizuho's top pick features very favorable partner checks, with strong demand for data warehousing and data modernization serving as significant growth drivers. The firm notes that CoCo adoption continues to broaden impressively, with use cases expanding beyond migrations and data modeling into semantic layers, observability, and AI app development. Mizuho expects another quarter of better-than-average product revenue upside and maintains a $425 price target.
2. Zscaler (ZS) - Quarterly checks showed improvement for a second consecutive quarter. Despite growing competition, ZS continues to be widely viewed as a best-in-class SASE/Zero Trust vendor. Mizuho believes the company can show more ARR upside to the Street than seen in recent quarters and maintains a $235 price target.
3. CrowdStrike (CRWD) - Checks were generally robust, including excellent large deal activity, continued strong adoption of Falcon Flex, and encouraging data points for the new Falcon Guardian module. Mizuho expects meaningful upside to ARR forecasts of $6.19 billion that call for nearly 26% year-over-year growth. The firm maintains a $275 price target despite the stock's 93% year-to-date gain.
4. Palo Alto Networks (PANW) - Momentum remains impressive, with particular strength in XSIAM, Prisma SASE, and Cortex subscription offerings. Partners observed a spike in pull-forward activity on the firewall side. Mizuho believes Total RPO will nicely exceed consensus estimates of 34-35% year-over-year and maintains a $415 price target.
5. Salesforce (CRM) - Inputs remain mixed overall, though customer upsells were solid and several renewal deals in the tens of millions of dollars of ACV were identified. Mizuho believes constant currency cRPO results can solidly exceed management's 14% year-over-year guidance, with a boost from recent acquisitions of Fin and Contentful. The firm maintains a $280 price target.
